brief: UBS's Thought of the Day: the 10-year Treasury yield swung from an intraday high of 5.34% (highest since 2002) to a close 4bps lower at 5.24%, as dovish comments from Fed officials Jefferson, Bowman and Williams cut the market-implied odds of an October hike to 30% from 70%. Resilient labor data (197,000 initial claims, 1.7mn continuing claims, August payrolls +162,000) and cooling core PCE (2.05% three-month annualized) support UBS's base case of one more hike in December then a 2027 hold, which lets equities absorb moderately higher rates in UBS's view. UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% this year and 14% in 2027. Separately, France's 2027 budget (5% deficit target, EUR43bn consolidation) widened the French-German spread 14bps, the most since March 2020, and the Italian spread 16bps. UBS reads limited market reaction plus solid auction demand as reassurance against a near-term funding crisis, and expects the resulting tightening in financial conditions to reduce the need for extended ECB hikes, with one more 25bp move expected in December. UBS also sees EURUSD, near 1.1214, as skewed toward recovery toward 1.15-1.20 and favors building euro exposure near current levels.
